property_summary: A single Put call should set unlockTime to the maximum of _unlockTime and block.timestamp; the mutant always sets it to block.timestamp, so subsequent calls with a larger future _unlockTime will show a lower unlockTime in the mutant.

After two Put calls where the second _unlockTime is strictly greater than the first and both are in the future, the reference unlockTime equals the second _unlockTime while the mutant unlockTime equals block.timestamp of the second call, which is less.

After a Put call and before any withdrawal, the unlockTime for the caller's account must be >= block.timestamp of the Put call and, if _unlockTime is in the future, must be >= _unlockTime; the mutant sets unlockTime = block.timestamp, violating the >= _unlockTime part when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.
After a Put with _unlockTime > block.timestamp, the caller's Acc.unlockTime must be exactly _unlockTime; the mutant sets it to block.timestamp instead.
After a Put call with a future _unlockTime, the caller's Acc.unlockTime must be strictly greater than block.timestamp; the mutant sets it to block.timestamp, breaking this.

After Put, the unlock time must be at least block.timestamp (the reference enforces this by clamping; the bug sets it to an arbitrary _unlockTime, allowing past timestamps, which immediately unlocks funds).
After any Put, an account's unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp at that time; the bug allows a past unlockTime, enabling immediate early Collect of the entire balance.

For any sender and any call value, after Put(_unlockTime) the account's unlockTime must be at least the Put's block.timestamp; the bug allows a smaller _unlockTime, making it possible to trigger an immediate early Collect of the whole balance if block.timestamp exceeds that past unlockTime.

After any Put, the account's unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp at the time of the Put call; the mutant sets unlockTime = _unlockTime unconditionally, allowing it to be a past timestamp, which makes funds immediately collectible.

After a Put with _unlockTime ≤ block.timestamp, calling Collect with _am ≤ balance should succeed for the reference (because unlockTime is clamped to block.timestamp, so block.timestamp > block.timestamp initially fails, but after a block warp it succeeds), while the bug sets unlockTime to _unlockTime (past), allowing immediate Collect, so the rule is: after Put and a warp past both the original and new unlock times, a partial Collect must succeed for the reference; the bug can cause premature success before the intended time.

For any user, after any sequence of calls to Put(any timestamp), the unlockTime stored in Acc[user] must always equal the maximum timestamp ever passed to Put by that user (or block.timestamp if block.timestamp was larger). The mutant removes the assignment, so unlockTime retains its default value of 0 forever, breaking the property.

After any Put call, the unlockTime for the caller must be at least block.timestamp at the time of the call; the mutant leaves unlockTime at its previous value (possibly 0), so it can be less than block.timestamp.

After any Put call, the unlockTime for the caller must be strictly greater than the caller's unlockTime before the call (since _unlockTime is passed, or block.timestamp is used, each > old); the mutant leaves unlockTime unchanged, so it does not increase.

For any user, after calling Put with a new timestamp _unlockTime, a subsequent call to Collect of any amount succeeds only if block.timestamp exceeds the unlock time recorded; the mutant never updates unlockTime, so when the old unlockTime was 0 a Collect can succeed much earlier than intended, violating the rule that Collect must revert when block.timestamp <= acc.unlockTime.

For any caller, after a Put call with a given _unlockTime, the value of acc.unlockTime returned by Acc[caller] must equal the maximum of _unlockTime and block.timestamp; the mutant leaves unlockTime unchanged, so it can differ from this value.

After any call to Put, the unlockTime stored in Acc[msg.sender] must be >= block.timestamp, which the reference satisfies but the mutant violates by assigning a fixed far-future timestamp that is independent of block.timestamp and can be less than the current time for some future blocks.

For any sender and any unlockTime argument, after calling Put, the stored unlockTime must be equal to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant breaks this by storing a constant value that independent of the arguments.

For any sender and any _unlockTime argument, after a successful call to Put(_unlockTime), the stored unlockTime must equal max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp). The mutant breaks this by always storing 4102444800 regardless of the block timestamp or argument.

For any sender and any ether sent with Put, after calling Put the sender can successfully Collect their full balance when enough time passes (block.timestamp > stored unlockTime), but the mutant's far-future constant unlockTime forever prevents collecting even if the original unlockTime argument would have allowed it.

After any sequence of Put calls by any sender with any amount and unlockTime, and waiting until block.timestamp exceeds the unlockTime stored for that sender, calling Collect with the full balance must succeed (not revert); the mutant's fixed far-future unlockTime makes Collect always revert in that state.

After any Put call, the sum of all holders' balances must equal address(c).balance; the bug removes overflow protection so an attacker can overflow their balance arbitrarily, making the sum exceed address(c).balance.
After every Put, any holder's balance strictly equals the total Ether they sent across all Puts, modulo 2^256, but the bug allows overflow to set a balance greater than the sum of their deposits.

After any sequence of Put calls, a holder's balance must never exceed the total value they have sent, but the buggy contract allows overflow to make a holder's balance arbitrarily larger than their total deposits.

For any caller, after a successful Put, the caller's balance must be at most the sum of their previous balance and the msg.value sent, but the bug allows overflow to make the new balance less than the previous balance (a decrease on addition), violating the monotonicity of balance under deposit.
After any sequence of Put calls, the sum of all Acc balances must equal the total Ether deposited, but the buggy version allows overflow to make the total balance exceed the contract balance.
Collect must never reduce the contract's Ether balance when called without a prior Payable deposit by the caller.
Collect must revert if the caller's unlock time has not been reached.

property_summary: Collect must only decrease a holder's balance when the caller has sufficient balance (>= MinSum and >= _am) and the lock time has passed; the mutant allows draining a holder's balance unconditionally.

For any caller, a Collect that transfers Ether out must not leave the holder's balance lower than it was before the call minus the amount, unless all original conditions (balance>=MinSum, balance>=_am, unlocked) held; the mutant reduces balance unconditionally even when the call fails, violating the invariant.

A Collect call that attempts to send Ether must not change the caller's Acc.balance or emit a Log message if the external call fails; the bugged version reduces balance and emits a log even on failed transfer, violating this invariant.

For any caller, after a Collect that does not revert, the change in the caller's Acc.balance must equal -_am and a Log message must be emitted; the mutant can revert after reducing balance, leaving balance permanently reduced with no successful transfer or log.

A Collect call that reverts must never reduce the caller's Acc.balance or emit a Log.AddMessage; the mutant reduces balance (and logs if the Log call succeeds before the revert) even when the ether send fails, violating this invariant.
Collect must revert when called exactly at unlockTime
Collect must revert if called when block.timestamp equals the account's unlockTime.
Collect must revert when block.timestamp is not strictly greater than _unlockTime.
After Put then Collect, it must be that block.timestamp > _unlockTime or Collect reverted.
After Put then Collect, if block.timestamp <= _unlockTime then Collect must revert.
